question.body:
The function $g$ has derivatives of all orders for all real numbers. The Maclaurin series for $g$ is given by $g(x)= sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac((- 1)^(n) x^(n),2 e^(n)+ 3)$ on its interval of convergence.

(a) State the conditions necessary to use the integral test to determine convergence of the series $sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac(1,e^(n))$. Use the integral test to show that $sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac(1,e^(n))$ converges.

(b) Use the limit comparison test with the series $sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac(1,e^(n))$ to show that the series $g(1)= sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac((- 1)^(n),2 e^(n)+ 3)$ converges absolutely.

(c) Determine the radius of convergence of the Maclaurin series for $g$.

(d) The first two terms of the series $g(1)= sum_(n = 0)^(oo) frac((- 1)^(n),2 e^(n)+ 3)$ are used to approximate $g(1)$. Use the alternating series error bound to determine an upper bound on the error of the approximation.
